newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy insurer Generali calm over Holocaust claims.
newsitem.headline: Italy insurer Generali calm over Holocaust claims.

text.p: Italy's Assicurazioni Generali said on Wednesday it was not worried that a request by an Israeli Holocaust research body to open its archives might lead to claims by victims' families over unpaid policies.

"We can't be held responsible after so many years. Other organisations took over from us in East European countries with the advent of communist regimes and it is to them that claims should be made," a Generali spokesman told Reuters.
He added that Generali's plan to take control of Migdal, the Israeli government-owned Bank Leumi's insurance arm, in which it holds a minority stake, would not be affected.

The Financial Times newspaper on Wednesday reported that Generali was being pressed by Yad Vashem, the Israeli-based Holocaust research institute, to open files on possibly tens of thousands of former customers who were murdered by the Nazis.
It said release of the files could open the door for a flood of claims against Generali by Holocaust victims and their descendants who have not received proceeds from policies.

The newspaper also said that a lawyer representing 15 families seeking proceeds of victims' insurance policies was pressing Israeli authorities to delay the Migdal deal until some compensation was agreed.

"The Migdal operation is continuing. There are a few administrative details to finalise but we are not worried that the deal may be blocked," the Generali spokesman said. "The deal should be concluded in a few weeks," he added.
